title: MediEvil
subtitle: A second chance for a false hero
summary: MediEvil is Sony's PlayStation action-adventure, first released in Europe on 9 October 1998. Sir Daniel Fortesque is remembered as Gallowmere's great champion, although he actually fell to the first arrow of the battle that made his reputation. When the sorcerer Zarok returns a century later, his magic accidentally revives Dan along with the dead. The skeletal knight now has a chance to earn the legend attributed to him. His journey mixes Halloween creatures and comic misfortune, making the unlikely hero's awkward appearance part of the adventure rather than an obstacle to it.
body: MediEvil is Sony's PlayStation action-adventure, first released in Europe on 9 October 1998. Sir Daniel Fortesque is remembered as Gallowmere's great champion, although he actually fell to the first arrow of the battle that made his reputation. When the sorcerer Zarok returns a century later, his magic accidentally revives Dan along with the dead. The skeletal knight now has a chance to earn the legend attributed to him. His journey mixes Halloween creatures and comic misfortune, making the unlikely hero's awkward appearance part of the adventure rather than an obstacle to it.

Dan fights with swords, clubs, crossbows and other weapons, some of which can be charged for stronger attacks. A club can also open a route, giving equipment a role in exploration. With nothing else available, Dan can detach his own arm and use it to strike or throw. Shields offer protection but wear out, so defence consumes another limited resource. Gargoyle heads provide advice or sell ammunition and services. The collection of tools turns each level into a question of what to spend, what to preserve and which object might reveal a passage.

Defeating enough suitable enemies fills a level's Chalice of Souls. Leaving with it opens a visit to the Hall of Heroes, where its residents can reward Dan with new weapons. The optional collection therefore reinforces his attempt to become a real hero, while Life Bottles increase how much punishment he can survive. Chris Sorrell and Jason Wilson developed the game's character and setting, accompanied by Andrew Barnabas and Paul Arnold's score. MediEvil 2 followed in 2000; later reinterpretations returned to this first adventure on PSP and PlayStation 4.
